questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice of the following sentence: 'The teacher is explaining the grammar rule to the students.'
options: The grammar rule is being explained to the students by the teacher.
The students are explained the grammar rule by the teacher.
The grammar rule was explained to the students by the teacher.
The grammar rule has been explained to the students by the teacher.
questions.explanation: In present continuous tense ('is explaining'), the passive voice structure is 'is/am/are + being + past participle'. Hence, 'is being explained' is correct.
questions.subject: English Language

questions.question: Match the idioms in Column I with their correct meanings in Column II:
questions.explanation: Once in a blue moon means very rarely; Spill the beans means reveal a secret; Burn the midnight oil means work/study late; Break the ice means start a conversation.
columnII: (III) Start a conversation in a tense situation
(IV) Work or study late into the night
questions.subject: English Language

questions.question: Directions: Given below are Assertion [As] and Reason [R]. Choose the correct option:
options: Both [As] and [R] are true, and [R] is the correct explanation of [As].
Both [As] and [R] are true, but [R] is not the correct explanation of [As].
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is singular, so it should take the singular verb 'was' instead of 'were'. Therefore, both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.
questions.assertion: The sentence 'Neither of the boys were present at the meeting' is grammatically incorrect in standard formal English.
questions.reason: Pronouns like 'neither', 'either', and 'each' are singular and must be followed by a singular verb.
questions.subject: English Language

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Direct and Indirect Speech and select the correct option:
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is incorrect because universal truths and habitual facts do NOT change their tense even when the reporting verb is in the past tense. Statements 1, 3, and 4 are correct rules of Narration.
statements: When the reporting verb is in the past tense, all present tenses inside the direct speech are changed to the corresponding past tense.
Universal truths and habitual facts undergo a change of tense even if the reporting verb is in the past tense.
Pronouns of the first person in direct speech change according to the subject of the reporting verb.
Words expressing nearness in time or place are changed into words expressing distance in indirect speech.
questions.subject: English Language

questions.question: Identify the one-word substitution for: 'A person who knows everything or has infinite knowledge.'
questions.explanation: 'Omniscient' means knowing everything. Omnipotent means all-powerful, omnipresent means present everywhere, and philanthropist means a lover of mankind.
questions.subject: English Language

questions.question: Rearrange the following parts (P, Q, R, S) to form a meaningful sentence:
questions.explanation: Subject 'the weary travelers' (R) comes first, followed by participle modifier 'walking cautiously' (Q), then prepositional phrase 'through the dark forest' (P), and finally the main verb predicate 'finally reached the safety of the village' (S). Thus, R → Q → P → S.
statements: S: finally reached the safety of the village

questions.explanation: Dis- forms Dishonest, Im- forms Impolite, In- forms Inactive, and Un- forms Unhappy. Hence, a-II, b-I, c-IV, d-III.

questions.question: Find out which part of the following sentence has an error: 'Scarcely had I stepped out of the house (A) / when a heavy downpour started (B) / and soaked me completely (C) / to the skin (D).'
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically sound. 'Scarcely' is correctly followed by 'had I stepped' (inversion) and paired with 'when'. There is no error in any part.
questions.subject: English Language

questions.question: Directions: Given below are Assertion [As] and Reason [R]. Choose the correct option:
options: Both [As] and [R] are true, but [R] is not the correct explanation of [As].
Both [As] and [R] are true, and [R] is the correct explanation of [As].
questions.explanation: We say 'have lunch', not 'have a lunch'. This is because meal names in a general sense take zero article, which aligns with general rules for unspecific nouns.
questions.assertion: Articles are not used before names of meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) used in a general sense.
questions.reason: Uncountable abstract nouns and general meal times generally take the zero article unless specified by a particular adjective or modifying clause.
questions.subject: English Language

questions.question: Choose the synonym of the word: 'METICULOUS'
questions.explanation: 'Meticulous' means showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise. 'Scrupulous' is its closest synonym. Careless is an antonym, audacious means bold.
questions.subject: English Language
